The all-chord threshold identifies a high-dimensional norm plateau that survives adding every missing pair, with each threshold tending uniformly to 1 even at maximal Hamming distance. The exact pointwise-to-norm separation grows as \(d-1/4\), a substantive interaction between graph geometry and operator-ideal norms not supplied by the base cube norm or cyclic analogues. This is a natural exact invariant, not a tiny numeric gain.
